core_obligations: Record that the equivalence of the two formulations is immediate (proof lines 5489).

Geometric route: translate the equivalent conditions into representability of the corresponding morphism of affine formal algebraic spaces, and conclude all three locality axioms from locality of that condition on source and target (proof lines 5490-5498).

Algebraic route, first axiom: given a diagram of the required shape, note that the comparison arrows satisfy the condition, and for a weak ideal of definition of the base trace its closure in the target and in the extension of the target, showing that as the chosen ideal runs over a fundamental system so do the closures, which gives the axiom (proof lines 5500-5519).

Algebraic route, second axiom: assume faithful flatness of the extension and the condition for the composite, show that the closure of the ideal generated by a weak ideal of definition of the base is open by computing the intersection of the target with the corresponding closed ideal of the extension in three steps, the third resting on faithful flatness, and identify the result as the closure of the ideal generated by the chosen one (proof lines 5521-5546).

Algebraic route, second axiom, conclusion: use topological nilpotence of the elements of that closure to see that it is a weak ideal of definition, and use the condition for the comparison arrow to get the reverse containment, so that the condition holds for the original arrow (proof lines 5544-5548).
Supply the proof of the third locality axiom, which the author declines to give here after having obtained it by the geometric route (proof line 5549).

difficulty_reason: For an arrow of complete weakly admissible topological rings, the lemma states the equivalence of tautness with the existence of a compatible inverse system of quotients whose limit is the target, and adds that this condition satisfies the three locality axioms (statement lines 5465-5487). The proof is notable for giving the locality twice by different means. The first is geometric: by an earlier lemma the equivalent conditions translate into representability of the corresponding morphism of affine formal algebraic spaces by algebraic spaces, and since that condition is etale local on source and target all three axioms follow at once (proof lines 5489-5498). The second is algebraic and is carried out for two of the three axioms. For the first axiom the closures of the ideals generated by a weak ideal of definition of the base are traced through the two arrows, and the observation that as the chosen ideal runs over a fundamental system so do its closures is what gives the axiom (proof lines 5504-5519). For the second axiom the argument is a genuine computation: assuming faithful flatness of the extension and the condition for the composite, the intersection of the target with the closed ideal is rewritten in three steps -- using the description of a fundamental system of neighbourhoods of zero by kernels, and then faithful flatness -- to become the intersection of the ideals generated by the chosen ideal of the base with a system of ideals of definition, which is exactly the closure of the ideal generated by the chosen one; openness of that closure then gives the axiom (proof lines 5521-5548). The claim is H3: the geometric route and the algebraic route are independent arguments, and within the algebraic route the second axiom needs a three-step identification whose middle step rests on faithful flatness.
